thread:
mike: RFC follow-up: proposing a 'debt-slab' strategy to incrementally extract runtime responsibilities into small modules over 12 weeks. doc: https://redwood/internal/rfc/debt-slab (summary below)

mike: TL;DR - split by capability slices (kv-cache, session-mesh, routing) into ~2-3 week slabs, each slab: extract module, add facade shim, run compatibility tests, canary, cutover. goal: reduce blast radius + make ownership explicit.

anya: smart. quick q: how do we guarantee API stability between facade and extracted module?

mike: we keep facade in place and only move implementation. contract tests + consumer-driven test harness run in CI. if mismatch, canary fails. we add a 'compat-mode' header to force old codepath during rollout.

sasha: DB concern: some slabs will need schema changes. migration plan? rolling migrations are risky.

rahul: suggest apply the strangler + sidecar pattern where the new module talks to a new schema namespace, replicate writes for a period, then backfill reads. avoids big-bang.

mike: agreed. proposed migration checklist in the doc:

```
- feature flag gating
- dual-write for 2 weeks
- read-backfill (batch job) verified by rowcounts and checksum
- small-window cutover with read-only fallback
- run consumer contract suite post-cutover
```

anya: Can we get a matrix of slabs -> owners -> tenant impact? we need to coordinate with Dedicated customers.

mike: yes, will add. initial owners mapped: kv-cache -> sasha, session-mesh -> rahul, request-router -> anya. Dedicated customers flagged for opt-in during canary.

sasha: perf note: extracting KV cache out-of-process adds IPC latency. need microbenchmarks to ensure we don't break 99th pct targets.

rahul: we can colocate the module with runtime on the same node for low-latency slabs; add grpc with unix sockets by default. config example:

```
module_sidecar:
  transport: ipc_unix
  socket_path: /var/run/sidecar-kv.sock
  max_inflight: 512
```

mike: good point. metric targets will be part of each slab's acceptance criteria: p50/p95/p99, token throughput, memory delta.

anya: how do we handle feature flags/rollbacks? quick rollback must be one command.

mike: design: 1) facade stays as single binary and toggles implementation via env/flag; 2) CI publishes a rollback job that flips flag + redeploy if canary alarms trip. documented runbook included.

infra-bot: CI pipeline update: job `slab-contract-tests` added to `main` that runs consumer tests in parallel for each slab. see pipeline: https://ci.internal/pipelines/1234

deploy-bot: Canaries will be scheduled to start 2025-06-16 09:00 UTC for kv-cache slab once microbenchmarks pass.

sasha: +1 to the plan. want a short PoC first — extract a tiny helper that currently lives in runtime and run it as sidecar for 2 weeks. low risk.

mike: yep PoC aligned. next steps: update RFC with owners, add migration matrix, schedule PoC for next sprint. I'll post a smaller checklist and assign tasks in JIRA.

anya: thanks — will prep the contract harness and cross-region routing test next week.

rahul: I'll draft the backfill jobs and perf harness.

mike: awesome. tagging @eng-sre to watch canary alarms and rollback hooks.

sasha: small nit — add observability for RPC-level token counts so we can attribute costs after extraction.

mike: noted. will add sensor events and billing tags to the slab acceptance criteria.

mike: end of thread — will update doc and ping again when PoC PR lands. :thumbsup:
